name: projects
description: Projects & Translations: 73 Catholic digital projects with AI-assisted work labelled (flagged entries excluded).

records.name: Aquinas Institute — Opera Omnia online (aquinas.cc)
records.license: Free to read online; print edition sold (copyright held)
records.languages: Latin -> English (also Polish and other parallel editions)
records.description: A human-translated, parallel Latin-English edition of Aquinas's complete works, free online and in print.
records.texts: Complete works of St. Thomas Aquinas in parallel Latin-English: Summa, Sentences, biblical commentaries, disputed questions, and more

records.name: Aquinas Institute — Augustine online (augustinus.cc)
records.description: The Aquinas Institute's parallel Latin-English Augustine reader.

records.name: Mediatrix Press — Bellarmine Translation Project
records.description: A long-running human translation effort that publishes St. Robert Bellarmine's works in English.

records.name: Freddoso — New English Translation of the Summa Theologiae

records.name: Ipsissima Verba

records.name: Franciscan Archive

records.name: Logic Museum

records.name: St. Thomas Aquinas's Works in English (isidore.co)

records.name: Updated Works — Patrologia Latina in English
records.license: Translations given away free (paid audiobooks); no formal license seen
records.description: Aims to translate the entire Patrologia Latina into English, then into modern English, and release it free.
records.texts: All 217 volumes of the Patrologia Latina, released volume by volume from Vol. 1
records.ai_detail: unclear (the page talks about AI reach but I did not confirm its translation method)
records.note: Self-described as modernizing 'primarily Christian' books; not Catholic-specific

records.name: Opera Savonaroliana
records.description: A society promoting Savonarola's canonization that is producing an English translation of his complete works.
records.texts: Savonarola's opera omnia; the site describes 'the first-ever English translation'
records.note: Savonarola is contested: he was excommunicated in 1497, and his cause was opened in 1997. The site exists to advocate his canonization. Present neutrally.

records.name: Migne.app — Patrologia Latina & Graeca, open
records.license: Latin/Greek public domain; English CC BY-NC 4.0 (per /method page)
records.description: Open reader for the whole of Migne, searchable by citation (e.g. 'PL 139, 473A'), with new English translations including many first-ever ones.
records.texts: All 387 vols of Migne (PL 1-221, PG 1-161), full Latin/Greek with citable column refs; English added work by work, with priority on 73 authors it says have never been translated.
records.ai_detail: yes: LLM-drafted under a rulebook, then checked partly by machine and partly by a human (site says so)

records.name: Lapide.org — Cornelius a Lapide commentary translated
records.license: Site calls its English 'public domain'. The GitHub repo has no license file.
records.languages: Latin -> English, plus ~35 other languages (Spanish, French, Portuguese, Tagalog, Swahili, Chinese, etc.)
records.description: AI (Claude) translation of the whole Lapide commentary into English and many other languages, with search and EPUBs. Content is going through a quality-control pass, and you can report errors as GitHub issues.
records.texts: Cornelius a Lapide SJ's Great Commentary on Scripture, plus other Latin works (Adam of Dryburgh, Riccioli, Sixtus of Siena, Pererius). EPUB downloads.

records.name: Bonaventure — Opera Omnia in English
records.license: English translation CC BY-NC 4.0 (© 2026, per the site footer); Latin public domain
records.description: The first complete English Opera Omnia of St. Bonaventure, drafted with an LLM from the Quaracchi Latin and checked against the printed page using a documented procedure.
records.texts: Quaracchi critical edition. Vol. I-IV (the full Commentary on the Sentences) and Vol. V (Breviloquium, Itinerarium, Collationes in Hexaemeron, disputed questions, sermons) are complete. Vol. VI scriptural commentaries in progress; the aim is all 10 volumes.
records.ai_detail: yes: LLM-drafted, then checked by a written procedure

records.name: ScholaThomistica
records.license: Not stated on the pages checked (source texts are public domain)
records.description: A free community library that turns public-domain Scholastic scans into clean, searchable Latin texts, adds translations, and lets contributors help repair the text.
records.texts: Scholastic philosophy and theology after Aquinas: Bañez, Salmanticenses, Ferrariensis, Denis the Carthusian, Alan of Lille, John of St. Thomas, Cajetan, Billuart and others. PDF/EPUB downloads.
records.ai_detail: yes: vision models for transcription, AI-assisted translation, human contributors

records.name: Mind of the Church
records.license: Free to read and download (no formal license seen)
records.description: New free library of Latin Catholic works translated into English for the first time, with a dedicated moral-theology site announced.
records.texts: Counter-Reformation commentaries and treatises. It starts with Sixtus of Siena's Bibliotheca Sancta (OT annotations, first English translation). Promised next: moral-theology manuals (Merkelbach, Noldin, Tanquerey, Vermeersch) and St. Antoninus.
records.ai_detail: yes: AI-assisted per the maintainer's X posts

records.name: Via Patrum
records.license: Free to read and listen; EPUB/PDF/audiobook downloads need a $50 library pass
records.description: Free library of the early Fathers in new modern English, translated with AI help and checked against the source. Each work names the edition it follows.
records.texts: 372 early-Church works (14,059 of 20,708 sections translated, per its About page), with the Greek/Latin one tap away, audio, topic and timeline views.
records.ai_detail: yes: AI-assisted, checked against the source (site says so)

records.name: Historical Christian Faith (writings and commentary databases)
records.license: Calls itself public domain; Commentaries repo license shows NOASSERTION on GitHub
records.description: Open, searchable databases of early Christian writings and commentary verse by verse, kept on GitHub and built to be reused.
records.texts: Verse-by-verse patristic commentary database plus a writings database. Some new public-domain AI translations, e.g. Bede on Acts. Second repo: HistoricalChristianFaith/Writings-Database.

records.name: @ViaEximii: Baroque Thomist and controversialist translations (Internet Archive)
records.license: Some items marked Public Domain Mark 1.0 (e.g. the De Anima and Billuart predetermination items); most have no license set
records.description: The most prolific individual translator of Baroque scholastics and Counter-Reformation controversialists on X. Uploads are free on the Internet Archive's opensource collection; several say they are AI-assisted (Claude).
records.texts: About 18 Internet Archive uploads (2024-2026) by the same translator: John of St. Thomas (Cursus Philosophicus: Logic, De Anima, Generation & Corruption; Defense of the Trinity; Essence/Existence/Subsistence), Gonet (Manuale Thomistarum vols. I-IV, Physical Premotion, Efficacy of the Divine Will), Billuart (Middle Knowledge, Divine Predetermination), Melchior Cano (De Locis Theologicis), Cornaeus (Ens Rationis Luthero-Calvinicum, 2026-07-27), Erbermann (Bellarmine Vindicated, 2026-08-09). Related uploads I could not attribute: Elorduy on Suárez's beatification (2026-08-18), Billuart Sermons ('translated with Sonnet 5'), Billuart on the Trinity, Clypeus Theologiae Thomisticae.
records.ai_detail: yes for several items (descriptions say 'AI translation'; translator credits Claude)

records.name: Patristica.jp — Patrologia Latina in Japanese
records.license: Not stated in the excerpt read
records.description: Parallel Latin-Japanese PL texts, translated by Claude and reviewed by a second LLM. The site says plainly that no human expert has checked them.
records.texts: PL works with Latin-Japanese parallel text, starting with Tertullian (PL 1). The site reports 409 works and 126,522 sections, citable by Migne column.
records.ai_detail: yes: Claude translation plus LLM review, no human expert check (site says so)

records.name: Bibliothecarius Modernus — Latin Patristic Texts (AI-assisted)
records.description: CC0 plain-text AI-assisted English translations of 225 PL texts, published as a searchable Jekyll site.
records.texts: 225 Latin patristic and medieval texts from the Patrologia Latina (2nd-13th c.), with English side by side
